# v0.29.2-rc1 — compaction gets past the scan limit and keeps exit headroom, and shutdown waits for it

This is the first release candidate for v0.29.2, a patch release on v0.29.1 and the first release train: it carries every fix that was ready when the train was cut. It fixes two compaction problems, one that could keep compaction from forming a summary on long tool-heavy sessions and one that could push the next request over the model's window. It also makes shutdown wait for a running compaction, stores a repeated tool call on hosts that reuse tool-call IDs, opens a profile's storage only when that profile is used, and lets the host open the bundled skill.

It adds one setting, `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S`. The schema version stays 5, and v0.29.1 remains the latest stable release until this candidate passes its gates (see **Qualification**).

## Changes since v0.29.1

### Compaction

- **A contiguity stop at the scan limit no longer repeats on every pass.** A claim on a chunk row stored above a later chunk row held back every row behind it. When the walk stopped first, at the leaf budget or at the scan limit, the leaf came out empty with the contiguity reason, and the next pass picked the same chunk, so some long tool-heavy sessions never formed a summary. v0.29.1's larger-budget retry cleared the budget case. Compaction now also retries once on the part of the chunk before the blocking row, ending on a tool-group boundary. The rows after that point stay in the host's context, and the existing escape summarises them from the store with tool pairs kept whole. A retry that would take a claim from a row it cut is refused, and the leaf stays as it was. The stop is logged once per conversation (`LCM contiguity hole:`, with IDs, roles and counts only) ([#1998](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1998), [PR #2032](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2032)).
- **An exit fit keeps its headroom when the list is over the window.** An automatic compaction exit fits the list under 95% of the host's threshold, so the next turn has room. When the list was also over the model's window budget, the fit dropped that cap and stopped at the window budget. On a 262,144-token model, the next request then landed above the host's threshold, every later turn started over it, and the provider finally rejected a request as over the window. The fit now first cuts whole oldest turns down to the exit budget, keeping the summary prefix and every recent row. When no whole-turn cut is deep enough, it behaves as before, and the next request can then still land above the host's threshold. Only the live list is shorter; stored rows are untouched ([#2039](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2039), [PR #2050](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2050)).

### Shutdown

- **Shutdown waits for a running compaction.** A host's `shutdown()` on another thread could close the databases under a running compaction, which could lose that pass or crash the worker. Shutdown now marks the engine as closing, waits up to `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` (default 10 s) for running passes to finish, and on a timeout logs one warning and leaves the connections open, so a later shutdown can close them. A running pass that sees the shutdown stops before its next write and returns the host's messages; writes it already committed stay committed. A pass that starts after shutdown began returns the host's messages unchanged and writes nothing ([#2101](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2101), [PR #2104](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2104)).

### Restarts and storage

- **A repeated tool call is stored when the host still shows the earlier one.** At the first turn after a restart, LCM-X proved a tool pair a replay by counting identical stored copies, including copies that the host's own history still shows before the point where matching resumes. On a host that reuses tool-call IDs, a new call and result that repeated an earlier pair exactly were then not stored. The copies the host's history accounts for are now set aside first, and a row recorded as a new occurrence is never skipped. When the earlier pair was compacted out of the host's view, the new pair can still be skipped (see **Known issues**) ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172), [PR #2185](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2185)).
- **A profile's storage opens on first real use.** Loading the plugin opened this profile's store right away, so another profile's gateway on the same host, which only loads the plugin, opened and held this profile's store and files. The store, its databases and the plugin's files now open on first real use, and a process that never uses a profile creates nothing for it. For the process's own home (the one `HERMES_HOME` names, or the default `.hermes` folder in the user's home when it is unset), the inactive-profile record is still written at load; `lcm_status` and `lcm_doctor` report it before storage opens ([#2152](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2152), [PR #2178](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2178)).

### Skill

- **The bundled skill opens with `skill_view`.** The plugin registered its skill folder instead of the skill file, so the host's `skill_view` tool failed on every operating system. It now registers `SKILL.md`. Capture, recall and compaction were not affected ([#571](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/571), [#2131](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2131), [PR #729](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/729)).

### Testing improved

- **New regression tests:** the contiguity-stop shapes and the prefix retry; the exit-fit headroom; shutdown during a compaction (a blocked pass, a timeout, passes that start while closing, and ingest that keeps running); a reused tool-call ID at a restart, with the compacted case pinned as a strict expected failure; 23 lazy-storage cells; and the registered skill path.
- **CI on release branches:** CI now runs on pushes and pull requests to `release/v*.x` maintenance branches, so each release-train head is checked without a manual run ([#2171](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2171), [PR #2190](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2190)).

## On by default in this release

Every change above is on by default. The one new setting, `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S`, sets how long shutdown waits for a running compaction. Local semantic recall stays on by default, as in v0.29.0.

## Upgrade

- **Host:** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is still required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer.
- **Store:** the schema version stays 5, with no new tables, columns or triggers.
- **Settings:** one added. `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` (seconds, default `10.0`, environment only) bounds how long shutdown waits for a running compaction. Invalid, negative and non-finite values use `10.0`, and values above `86400` are capped there.
- **From v0.29.0 or older:** follow the v0.29.1 upgrade notes first, including its note on the first restart after the upgrade.
- **Rollback:** target `v0.29.1`, which ignores the new setting. Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`), and compare ordered raw messages and summary provenance through upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade.

## Known issues

- **Some compaction passes still write no summary** ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880)): a pass that forms no summary input (a tool group the host keeps half of, a contiguity stop, or rows with no stored source) writes no summary but still returns a rebuilt copy of the host's list, which the host commits. Returning the host's original list on such passes is planned for v0.30.0, because the fix tried for this release did not pass review. It matters because, on the reference agent, one such pass made the host rewrite its history and rebuild its prompt cache. The contiguity stop that repeated on every pass of some long tool-heavy sessions is cleared for both known causes (see **Compaction** above); an ignored row just before the cut tool group, or a retry refused because it would take a cut row's claim, can still keep that shape stuck, no worse than v0.29.1; the ignored-row case's fix is part of the [#1993](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1993) design. Nothing is lost. On a group whose request stays above the preflight limit and whose only progress is on hidden rows, the escape can spend about 80 to 130 s on a pass the host cannot use before a cold turn's first reply (first output came at about 95 to 162 s on the reference agent, on first turns after restarts). Moving this work out of the wait before a reply is planned for v0.30.0 ([#2173](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2173)).
- **Survival-fit rotations leave no compaction record:** when a session rotates because the survival fit trimmed the live view, the new session gets no record of what the previous one compacted, so rows stored under earlier sessions may not be matched to their stored copies. A compaction that is already blocked on such rows can then stay blocked, and while it is blocked each survival fit trims older rows from what the model sees with no summary in their place. Its frequency on its own is unknown. No stored rows are lost: the store keeps every row and recall can still reach them. A fix is tracked for v0.30.0 ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Slow summaries can shrink the live view:** when summary calls time out at the compaction threshold, the survival fit can drop about 80–115 older rows from what the model sees. The store keeps every row and recall can still reach them; a fix is tracked for the compaction-you-don't-notice release ([#2004](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2004)).
- **The exit fit's headroom cut can drop rows no summary covers** ([#2184](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2184)): when an automatic exit fit is over the window budget, the cut this release adds takes whole old turns out of the model's view down to the exit budget, and it can take rows no summary covers. On the reported shape that is about 36,000 tokens more than the window alone needs. The store keeps every row and recall can still reach them. A fix that drops covered rows first is planned for v0.30.0.
- **Catalog install on upstream Hermes with the plugin scanner:** the upstream catalog entry pins the v0.29.0 payload. An update to v0.29.1's payload is proposed ([Hermes #148452](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/148452)), and an update to this release's payload follows its GA. Until then, a catalog install gets an older release; use `scripts/install.sh` for this release. Hermes v0.22.6 and newer rate v0.29.1's payload `safe`: their scanner counts the small-host CPU detector's read-only `/proc/self` reads as low severity ([Hermes #146352](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/146352)), and this release does not change that detector. Hermes v0.22.5 and older rate it `caution` (not `safe`) for those reads; nothing was changed to hide them from the scanner ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946)). Hermes 0.21.3's scanner blocks a `caution` verdict from a community source, so a catalog install there needs `--force` after reviewing the findings, or `scripts/install.sh`.
- **Upstream Hermes manual `/compress`:** on Hermes stable releases up to v0.22.5, a manual `/compress` from the gateway uses the host's own compressor and bypasses LCM-X, so stored history can gain duplicate replies. No rows were lost in the reported cases. Upstream Hermes fixed this on its main branch on 2026-10-28 ([Hermes #145806](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145806), fixing [#143587](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143587)): `/compress` now runs the session's LCM-X engine. The LCM-X defence planned for v0.30.0 stays until the oldest supported Hermes includes the fix ([#1922](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1922), [#1924](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1924)).
- **Shutdown during a compaction, two edge cases** ([#2183](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2183)): if shutdown stops an overflow-recovery pass, the pass returns the host's list without fitting it and does not record that recovery failed; and if a pass had already committed leaves when shutdown stopped it, its status still reads `noop` ("engine shutting down"). Both need a shutdown to start during a pass. Stored rows are not affected.
- **Shutdown does not wait for an ingest outside a compaction** ([#2193](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2193)): an ingest started by the preflight check or by an `lcm_*` tool call is not counted as a running compaction, so a shutdown at that moment can close the store under it. That ingest then fails and rolls back, so nothing is written half-way and the host still holds the messages. It needs a shutdown at the same moment as such an ingest.
- **The inactive-profile record on another home layout** ([#2152](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2152)): when `HERMES_HOME` is unset and Hermes uses a platform default home other than the `.hermes` folder in the user's home, LCM-X treats the process's own home as another profile's. Its inactive-profile record is then kept in memory and written only at first real use, so a process that never uses storage does not save it; `lcm_status` and `lcm_doctor` in that process still report it. Stored messages are not affected.
- **Retry shapes still being fixed** (all are redesigned together for v0.30.0, including the two cases that can lose a row, #1837 and #1838):
  - after a tool call is retried with new message IDs, each later cold restart can store that call and its result again: one more copy per restart, nothing lost ([#1836](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1836));
  - after a cold restart, if only the tool result's message ID changes on a retry, the new result may not be stored ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837));
  - if the plugin restarts before a session's first compaction and the host re-sends the last tool turn with a new timestamp on its user message, that user message and its tool pair may not be stored ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838));
  - in some retry and restart sequences after compaction, a replaced or retried message can be dropped or stored twice ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
  Real-host frequency is unknown.
- **Crash before a reply, then rotation:** on hosts that do not give messages unique IDs, if the agent crashes before replying and the conversation then rotates, the next turn can be stored twice. A fix targets v0.30.0 ([#1508](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1508)).
- **Duplicates kept on purpose:** turns stored before v0.29.0's carried-stamp marker can be stored again by a replay, and user messages that the host itself mirrors after an ACP crash recovery are kept twice. LCM-X keeps both copies rather than risk losing a genuine message; see `docs/identity-ledger.md` ([#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501), [PR #1775](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1775)).
- **Restarts can store old rows again:** at a long conversation's first turn after a gateway restart, the host rebuilds the conversation and hands its assistant and tool rows to LCM-X without their timestamps, and LCM-X can store rows it already holds a second time, as on v0.28.x, v0.29.0 and v0.29.1. Nothing is lost, but recall can show a row several times, one more copy per restart. A fix is planned for v0.30.0, because it builds on the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A restart can store a tool result again without its call:** at a session's first turn after a restart (a cold bind), if the point where LCM-X resumes matching falls between a tool call and its result, the result can be stored a second time without the call. Nothing is lost, and the copy is not sent to the model as a stored row (a result without its call is dropped from the model's context), but recall can show it twice. v0.29.0 and v0.29.1 behave the same. A fix is planned for v0.30.0 ([#2163](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2163)), because it needs the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds.
- **A restart can skip a repeated tool call after its earlier copy was compacted out** ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)): at a session's first turn after a restart, on a host that reuses tool-call IDs (for example `call_0` on every turn), a new tool call and result that exactly repeat a pair already compacted out of the host's view can be taken for a replay and not stored. The host keeps them, but LCM-X's store does not, so recall cannot find them. Hosts that give each tool call a unique ID, as the reference agent's host does, are not affected. This release fixes the case where the host still shows the earlier pair; the compacted case needs the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds.
- **A crash right after a rotation can keep an extra reply in tests:** the reliability test that kills the agent right after a rotation can count one stored reply as extra. In every run checked for v0.29.1, the host had saved that reply too, so LCM-X matched the host and nothing was lost; the test's kill timing and its scorer are being fixed ([#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861)). Whether the older reports in [#824](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/824) are the same test effect is still being checked.
- **Local embeddings on large, fully embedded stores (small hosts):** on a 2-CPU host with a 250,000-row fully embedded store, a semantic recall could use its full 8-second budget. Since v0.29.0, hosts with at most 2 effective CPUs answer from full text immediately when local embeddings are on by default (`degraded=true`, `cpu_limited`); explicit settings keep control. Faster exact semantic recall under contention is tracked in [#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586); the first attempt did not meet its memory bar, so no release is promised yet.
- **Local embeddings can outvote exact keyword hits:** with v0.29.0's deep-match fix, recall with embeddings off now returns its full 25 matches as well, and on the LoCoMo benchmark it answers more questions than the default local embeddings (1,165 vs 1,089 of 1,986 questions). Fusion gives the keyword arm half the weight of each embedding arm, so embedding-only hits can push an exact keyword hit out of the 25. Local embeddings still lead on LongMemEval-S (426 vs 408 of 500) and show no regression against v0.28.1. A fusion-weight change needs its own measurement and is planned for a minor release, not this patch ([#950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/950)).
- **Python only: switching an existing config object to a cloud provider:** if code changes `embedding_provider` to a cloud provider on an `LCMConfig` that already resolved to the local default (with `dataclasses.replace` or attribute assignment), the enabled setting carries over, and that provider starts receiving text without `embeddings_enabled=True`. Settings from the environment and new `LCMConfig(...)` objects are not affected. Set `embeddings_enabled` explicitly when you switch providers in code; a fix is tracked in [#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959).
- **Subagent work is not stored:** what a delegated subagent does in its own session, including its tool calls and intermediate results, is not stored by LCM-X. Only what the subagent returns to the parent conversation is stored, so `lcm_recall` cannot find a subagent's intermediate results. This isolation is not new in this release. Storing subagent sessions is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931)).
- **A restart at an unlucky moment around compaction can store one summary row again** ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286)): three narrower restart timings stay open. They are a restart after a cleanup-only pass that the host kept without signalling that it committed it; with the non-default `compression.in_place=false`, a restart after the host published the new session but before LCM-X saw it start; and a restart while a second compaction still waits for the host to adopt it. Each can store the summary text once more as a message. Nothing is lost, and all three are older than v0.29.0.
- **A repeated message on a host that does not send its full history** ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)): on a host that sends its full history at each turn, as the reference agent's host does, the lists below are replays after a restart, and storing nothing is correct. On a host that sends only new messages, or only its most recent ones, a message can be lost in two narrow cases, because the saved restart record can take a genuinely new message for a replay:
  - The record counts identical messages once, so a cleaned list that carries every distinct message since the last compaction, but fewer copies of a repeated one (a reply like "Done." given twice), counts as a replay of the conversation. A later batch of new messages that repeats every distinct message stored since that compaction can then be taken for a replay and not stored.
  - After a compaction, at a restart whose first list holds an older timestamped message and a new message without a timestamp, but not the rest of the session, LCM-X rewrites the record to that short list. After another restart, a new message identical to the untimestamped one, sent with the same older message, can be taken for a replay and not stored.

  Both cases come from the record v0.29.1 added; in them, v0.29.0 stores a second copy instead. Telling a replay from a genuine repeat on such hosts needs a record of which stored rows are duplicates, planned for v0.30.0.
- **Hosts whose messages carry no timestamps:** LCM-X recognises a replay at a restart only from timestamped messages. On such a host, a message inserted earlier in the list, or a list of only new unstamped messages, can still be stored again at each restart, as on v0.29.0. Nothing is lost. The reference agent's host timestamps its messages, except the assistant and tool rows it rebuilds at a restart (see the restart item above).
- **Restart duplicates v0.29.1's restart fix does not cover yet:** in a few rarer orders of events the saved record is not rewritten, so the next restart can store messages a second time, as before that fix; none loses a message ([#2115](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2115), [#2119](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2119)). When a host replaces an unstamped reply during a resend, or edits an unstamped assistant message in place, the new text is stored only at the next restart, along with a second copy of the conversation ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116), [#2117](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2117)). Two rarer passes that rewrite the host's list without changing which messages it holds, an overflow recovery and a compaction of only hidden rows, keep no saved record, as on v0.29.0, so a restart after one can store messages a second time ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **Summary obligations after an out-of-order row in a session started by a compaction:** a later summary may not be required to cover some of the parent session's messages. The messages stay in the store and recall can still reach them. This predates v0.29.0; a fix is tracked for v0.30.0 ([#2123](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2123)).
- **Cross-process cleanup:** another process sharing the store can still clear an empty live session binding and stall later compaction ([#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [#761](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/761)).
- **Extra rows in one degraded mode:** when a child compaction can never publish (a different case from a single failed publication), three runtime hosts store extra rows and repeat user tags. No user content is missing. That reliability cell now gates on missing content only ([#1797](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1797), [#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1929](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1929)).

## Qualification

This is a release candidate for testing. It is not qualified for general use yet, and v0.29.1 remains the latest stable release. As the first release train, v0.29.2 runs a smoke stage first at each release candidate, and no long row starts until it passes; then it runs the gauntlet rows its diff selects ([#1995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1995), [PR #2088](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2088)). This diff changes the engine and the plugin's entry point, so it selects every memory row. Where the release rules allow, rows reuse v0.29.1's baseline measurements from earlier runs; each receipt says so. The GA notes will report each row below with its receipt.

- Smoke stage: the reliability matrix, Phase A, the probe matrix, host cells and short versions of the long rows: **TBD**.
- Full suite, the CI way, at the rc tag: **TBD**.
- Phase B: independent review sweep of the full v0.29.1 → rc diff, pinned-host suites and the reliability matrix: **TBD**.
- Phase A: live all-tools matrix, cloud-default and local postures: **TBD**.
- Phase C on the real hosts, with the doctor bar: **TBD**.
- Local host cells: plugin-manager installs on two hosts, plus the floor host's manual and default setups ([#1970](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1970)): **TBD**.
- Local upgrade roundtrip (upgrade → rollback → re-upgrade): **TBD**.
- D1 recall changes in the shipped local default, with embeddings off recorded beside it: **TBD**.
- D4 question answering in the local default, D8 delivery guards and the A/A′ placebo: **TBD**.
- D2 facts kept, D3 Track S absolutes and D7 per-message wait: **TBD**.
- D5-B controlled clone: **TBD**.
- Not run: the D6 recorded rows (not selected for this patch).
